questions.question: The present age of a father is equal to sum of ages of his son and daughter. Ten years ago from now, the age of the father was double the age of the son and four times the age of the daughter. The total present age of the father, daughter and son is ____ years.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Father's age** 10 years ago be x. Then **Son's age** was x/2 and **Daughter's age** was x/4.

Present ages: Father = (x + 10), Son = (x/2 + 10), Daughter = (x/4 + 10).

Given: Present **Father** = **Son** + **Daughter** ⇒ (x + 10) = (x/2 + 10) + (x/4 + 10).

⇒ x + 10 = 3x/4 + 20 ⇒ x/4 = 10 ⇒ x = 40.

Present Father = 50. Since Total = Father + (Son + Daughter) and Father = Son + Daughter, Total = 2 × Father = 2 × 50 = 100.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the present ages of the **Father**, **Son**, and **Daughter** be **F**, **S**, and **D** respectively.

**Given:**

1) **F = S + D**

2) 10 years ago: **(F − 10) = 2(S − 10)** and **(F − 10) = 4(D − 10)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/158a77d6745795e2cb0424138d2cfefe981309704623b07ec0a9c5c4676d019e.png] 

From the second condition:

⇒ F − 10 = 2S − 20 ⇒ 2S = F + 10 ⇒ S = (F + 10) ÷ 2

⇒ F − 10 = 4D − 40 ⇒ 4D = F + 30 ⇒ D = (F + 30) ÷ 4

Substitute **S** and **D** in the first equation:

⇒ F = [(F + 10) ÷ 2] + [(F + 30) ÷ 4]

Multiply the entire equation by 4 to clear denominators:

⇒ 4F = 2(F + 10) + (F + 30)

⇒ 4F = 2F + 20 + F + 30

⇒ 4F = 3F + 50

⇒ **F = 50 years**

Calculating **S** and **D**:

⇒ S = (50 + 10) ÷ 2 = 30 years

⇒ D = (50 + 30) ÷ 4 = 20 years

**Total Age:**

⇒ Total = F + S + D = 50 + 30 + 20 = 100 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains **constant** at any point in time (past, present, or future).

Time Shift in Ages

If the current age is **x**, then age **n** years ago was (x − n) and age **n** years hence will be (x + n).

Ratio and Units Method

When ratios at two different times are given, ensure the **ratio difference** between the periods is scaled to match the actual **time gap**.

questions.question: Two positive numbers are in the ratio 2:3. If the product of their LCM and HCF is 294, then find the sum of the two numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 2 : 3

Product of ratio parts = 2 × 3 = 6 units²

Given product of **LCM and HCF** = 294

1 unit² = 294 ÷ 6 = 49 → 1 unit = √49 = 7

Sum of numbers = (2 + 3) × 7 = 5 × 7 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of two **positive numbers** = 2 : 3

Product of **LCM** and **HCF** = 294

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = **LCM** × **HCF**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8e4f378de7a2650caed2b5d193985e2977d98d96346fa99c165a3d6915a32df2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two positive numbers be 2x and 3x.

⇒ According to the property: (2x) × (3x) = 294

⇒ 6x² = 294

⇒ x² = 294 ÷ 6

⇒ x² = 49

⇒ x = √49 = 7

⇒ The numbers are: 2 × 7 = 14 and 3 × 7 = 21

⇒ Sum of the two numbers = 14 + 21 = 35

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Property of HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the relationship is always: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Ratio and HCF

If two numbers are in the ratio x : y, then the numbers can be written as Hx and Hy, where H is the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

LCM of Ratio Numbers

If the numbers are Hx and Hy (with x and y being coprime), then their **LCM** is H × x × y.

questions.question: Two trains, 130 meters and 120 meters long, are running in parallel tracks in the same direction at speeds of 62 km/hr and 44 km/hr, respectively. How much time will the faster train take to completely cross the slower one?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in **same direction** = 62 − 44 = 18 km/hr.

Convert speed to **m/s**: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s.

Total distance to cross = 130 + 120 = **250 m**.

Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 250 ÷ 5 = **50 sec**.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **faster train** (L₁) = 130 m

Length of the **slower train** (L₂) = 120 m

Speed of the **faster train** (S₁) = 62 km/hr

Speed of the **slower train** (S₂) = 44 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d8cbc543126ab68da7bc4fa3e11cd0170f1bce626b38070079c17c84833fd7dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance to be covered = 130 + 120 = 250 m

⇒ Relative speed of trains = 62 − 44 = 18 km/hr

⇒ Convert relative speed to m/s: 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

⇒ Time taken by the faster train = 250 ÷ 5 = 50 sec

The final calculated time is 50 sec, which corresponds to option (2).

**∴ The correct answer is 50 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **same direction**, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train or a platform, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum** of their respective lengths.

questions.question: Pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in 10 hours. Pipes, B and C, can fill the same tank in 20 hours. If pipe B alone can fill the same tank in 30 hours, how much time will the pipes A and C take together to fill the same tank.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** (LCM of 10, 20, 30) = 60 units.

Efficiency of (A+B) = 6, (B+C) = 3, and **Pipe B** = 2.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 6 − 2 = 4; Efficiency of **Pipe C** = 3 − 2 = 1.

Combined Efficiency of (A+C) = 4 + 1 = 5 units/hr.

Time taken = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 10 hr

Time taken by (B + C) = 20 hr

Time taken by **Pipe B** = 30 hr

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = Efficiency of (A+B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 6 − 2 = 4 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe C** = Efficiency of (B+C) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of **Pipe C** = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Combined Efficiency of **Pipe A** and **Pipe C** = 4 + 1 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Time taken by A and C together = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Filling pipes are considered to have **positive efficiency**, while emptying (leakage) pipes have **negative efficiency**.

Efficiency-Time Relationship

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken is x : y, the ratio of efficiency is y : x.

Combined Work Formula

If two pipes can fill a tank in x and y hours respectively, they together fill it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) hours.

questions.question: Chetan’s salary is ₹16000 per month. He spends ₹6000 on house rent, ₹1500 on bills and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings(in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday he spent his complete monthly saving for birthday celebration.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Monthly Savings** = 16000 − (6000 + 1500) = ₹8500

Savings for **11 months** (as 1 month's savings is spent on birthday) = 8500 × 11

Total Yearly Savings = 93500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹93500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Monthly Salary = **₹16000**

House Rent = **₹6000**

Monthly Bills = **₹1500**

**Formula:** Savings = Income − Expenditure

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4321c2fe6b1f2dce14e7f3283c61a64013d50daa574bb6ced796f6abcaa8dea1.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Total Monthly Expenditure = House Rent + Bills

⇒ Total Monthly Expenditure = 6000 + 1500 = **₹7500**

⇒ Monthly Savings = Salary − Expenditure

⇒ Monthly Savings = 16000 − 7500 = **₹8500**

⇒ Number of months in a year = 12

⇒ Savings are spent in 1 month (birthday month), so net savings occur for = 12 − 1 = **11 months**

⇒ Total Savings in a year = Monthly Savings × 11

⇒ Total Savings in a year = 8500 × 11

⇒ Total Savings in a year = **₹93500**

Therefore, the correct option is **(3)**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹93500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relationship

Income is always the sum of **Expenditure** and **Savings**. If any two are known, the third can be calculated using Income − Expenditure = Savings.

Annual Calculation

To convert monthly data to annual data, multiply by 12. If a specific period involves **extra spending** or **no savings**, adjust the multiplier accordingly (e.g., use 11 instead of 12).

Savings Percentage

Savings % = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. In this case, monthly savings % = (8500 ÷ 16000) × 100 = 53.125%.

**Simple Interest** for 6 years = 800 × 6 = ₹4,800.

**Total Amount** payable = **Principal** + **SI** for 6 years = 8,000 + 4,800 = ₹12,800.

∴ The correct answer is ₹12,800.</strong

questions.question: Surjeet buys 20 kg of sugar for ₹900. He sells 18 kg of sugar for ₹918. What is the percentage profit made by Surjeet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate unit price for both **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)**.

**CP** of 1 kg = 900 ÷ 20 = ₹45

**SP** of 1 kg = 918 ÷ 18 = ₹51

**Profit Percentage** = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100

Profit % = (6 ÷ 45) × 100 = 2/15 × 100 = 40/3% = 13(1/3)%

**∴ The correct answer is 13(1/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Cost Price (CP)** of **20 kg sugar** = ₹900

Total **Selling Price (SP)** of **18 kg sugar** = ₹918

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e92f2fa2fa8074a942636f389b24b6f01be2a1df6d43aaaac02c3e6f2994da2.png] 

**Formula used:**

Profit = **Selling Price** − **Cost Price**

Profit Percentage = (Profit ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 kg sugar = 900 ÷ 20 = ₹45

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** of 1 kg sugar = 918 ÷ 18 = ₹51

⇒ **Profit** per kg = 51 − 45 = ₹6

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (6 ÷ 45) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (2/15) × 100 = 200/15

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = 40/3 = 13(1/3)%

**∴ The correct answer is 13(1/3)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Profit % is always calculated on the CP unless otherwise stated.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

The fraction 1/15 is approximately equal to 6.66%. Thus, 2/15 = 2 × 6.66% = 13.33% or 13(1/3)%.

Unitary Method

To compare prices of different quantities, always find the value of a single unit (1 kg, 1 item, etc.) to simplify calculations.

questions.question:
324 × 24 = 7776.

What will 7.776 ÷ 2.4 be equal to?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

**324** × **24** = **7776**

**Formula used:**

**Dividend** ÷ **Divisor** = **Quotient**

**Calculations:**

From the given data:

⇒ 7776 ÷ 24 = **324**

We need to find the value of:

⇒ **7.776 ÷ 2.4**

Multiplying both the dividend and divisor by 10 to simplify the decimal:

⇒ (7.776 × 10) ÷ (2.4 × 10) = 77.76 ÷ 24

Expressing 77.76 as a fraction:

⇒ 77.76 ÷ 24 = (7776 ÷ 100) ÷ 24

Rearranging the terms:

⇒ (7776 ÷ 24) ÷ 100

Substituting the known value **7776 ÷ 24 = 324**:

⇒ 324 ÷ 100 = **3.24**

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: In a class, the average weight of the boys is 65 kg and the average weight of the girls is 45 kg. The average weight of the whole class is 57 kg. What is the ratio of the number of girls to the number of boys in the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **alligation method** using the average weights of **boys** (65) and **girls** (45) with the **class mean** (57).

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = (57 − 45) : (65 − 57) = 12 : 8

Simplifying the ratio: 12 : 8 = 3 : 2 (Boys : Girls)

The question asks for the ratio of **Girls to Boys**, which is 2 : 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average weight of **boys** = 65 kg

Average weight of **girls** = 45 kg

Average weight of the **whole class** = 57 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = (Average Weight × Number of Students)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cfe969a22ef3e3ed6321e8badd9385467afac09731cc06b0201cadf5bdb3b9c.png] 

Let the number of **boys** be 'B' and **girls** be 'G'.

⇒ Total weight of class = 57 × (B + G)

⇒ Also, Total weight = 65B + 45G

⇒ 57B + 57G = 65B + 45G

⇒ 57G − 45G = 65B − 57B

⇒ 12G = 8B

⇒ G ÷ B = 8 ÷ 12

⇒ G : B = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Rule

It is a rule that enables us to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at the given price must be mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Weighted Average Formula

The average of a combined group is given by Aₘ = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n represents the quantity and A represents the average of each group.

questions.question: A store offers a 10% festival discount on the marked price of ₹900. Later, to clear the stock, it offers an additional 5% off on the already discounted price. What is the total amount paid by the customer?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total amount paid using the **successive multiplier method**:

**Net Selling Price** = 900 × (90/100) × (95/100)

**Net Selling Price** = 900 × 0.9 × 0.95

**Net Selling Price** = 810 × 0.95 = ₹769.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹769.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹900, **First Discount** = 10%, **Additional Discount** = 5%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0aa8a8c1c3987bb33cece9a20a37a144ab19c274d5a4f6191149562ae8145eda.png] 

Step-by-step calculation:

⇒ **First discounted price** = 900 − (10% of 900)

⇒ **First discounted price** = 900 − 90 = ₹810

⇒ **Final amount paid** = 810 − (5% of 810)

⇒ **Final amount paid** = 810 − 40.50 = ₹769.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹769.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Single Equivalent Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

Selling Price is calculated as SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100. For successive discounts, multiply each reduction factor.

Successive Discounts with Fraction

If discounts are 10% (1/10) and 5% (1/20), the price becomes 9/10 and 19/20 of the original value respectively.

questions.question: A trader buys a mobile phone for ₹8000, spends ₹500 on repairs, and sells it at a profit of 20% on the total cost. Later, the buyer resells it at a loss of 25%. What price does the final buyer pay for the mobile phone?
questions.solution:

**Total Effective CP** = 8000 + 500 = ₹8500

Net multiplier for **20% profit** and **25% loss** = 1.20 × 0.75 = 0.9

Final Price = 8500 × 0.9 = ₹7650

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7650.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Purchase price of **mobile phone** = ₹8000

Amount spent on **repairs** = ₹500

Profit percentage = 20%

Loss percentage of the buyer = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = Cost Price + Overhead Expenses

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 or CP × (100 − Loss%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a90bee20f70764597131159ab163d251916df21d88f2427711735a0731c0adab.png] 

**Calculations:**

questions.question: The numerator of a fraction is 8 less than the denominator. If the denominator is increased by 5 and the numerator is increased by 3, we get the fraction (3)/(4). Find the original fraction.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check options based on the given conditions.

Condition 1: **Denominator − Numerator = 8**. For 27/35, 35 − 27 = 8 (Satisfied).

Condition 2: **(Numerator + 3) / (Denominator + 5) = 3/4**.

⇒ (27 + 3) / (35 + 5) = 30 / 40 = 3/4 (Satisfied).

**∴ The correct answer is 27/35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numerator = Denominator − 8

New Numerator = Numerator + 3

New Denominator = Denominator + 5

New Fraction = 3/4

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/403d1add19b44b711fd68260427414eb303b30422341cb4c102cb0b012103b59.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **denominator** of the original fraction be x.

⇒ **Numerator** = x − 8

⇒ Original Fraction = (x − 8) / x

According to the question:

⇒ ((x − 8) + 3) / (x + 5) = 3 / 4

⇒ (x − 5) / (x + 5) = 3 / 4

By cross-multiplication:

⇒ 4 × (x − 5) = 3 × (x + 5)

⇒ 4x − 20 = 3x + 15

⇒ 4x − 3x = 15 + 20

⇒ x = 35

Now, find the numerator:

⇒ Numerator = 35 − 8 = 27

⇒ Original Fraction = 27/35

**∴ The correct answer is 27/35.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proper and Improper Fractions

A **Proper Fraction** is one where the numerator is less than the denominator (e.g., 27/35). An **Improper Fraction** has a numerator greater than or equal to the denominator.

Equivalent Fractions

Fractions that represent the same value even though they look different, obtained by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number.

Cross-Multiplication Rule

In an equation like a/b = c/d, the property a × d = b × c is used to solve for unknown variables in linear equations involving fractions.

questions.question: From the top of a 75-meter-high lighthouse, the angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. If the two ships are on the same side of the lighthouse and in a straight line with its base, find the distance between the two ships. (Use √3 = 1.732)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance between two objects on the same side = **Height** × (cot θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ − cot θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ)

Distance = 75 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Distance = 75 × (√3 − 1) = 75 × (1.732 − 1)

Distance = 75 × 0.732 = 54.9 m

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the **lighthouse** (AB) = 75 m

**Angles of depression** of two ships = 30° and 45°

Since the ships are on the same side, the angles of elevation from the ships to the top are also 30° and 45°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/463e2afdf3a1b6805984aaece400a6e4cb610526c7494030d9265e37f3802f25.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right ΔABC (closer ship at C):

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 = 75 ÷ BC ⇒ BC = 75 m

⇒ In right ΔABD (farther ship at D):

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = 75 ÷ BD ⇒ BD = 75√3 m

⇒ Distance between ships (CD) = BD − BC

⇒ CD = 75√3 − 75 = 75(√3 − 1)

⇒ CD = 75 × (1.732 − 1) = 75 × 0.732

⇒ CD = 54.9 m

**∴ The correct answer is 54.9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal line for an object below the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance problems, tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base and cot θ = Base ÷ Perpendicular are most commonly used.

General Formula for Same Side

Distance d = h × |cot α − cot β|, where h is height and α, β are angles of elevation/depression.</p

questions.question: If the average of four numbers is 15, and three of the numbers are 10, 20, and 25, what is the fourth number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the **Net Deviation** method where the **Average** is 15.

Deviations of given numbers from 15: (10 − 15) = **−5**, (20 − 15) = **+5**, (25 − 15) = **+10**.

Sum of known deviations = −5 + 5 + 10 = **+10**.

To keep the average 15, the total deviation must be **0**; thus, the fourth number deviation = **−10**.

Fourth number = 15 − 10 = **5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of **4 numbers** = 15

Three numbers are 10, 20, and 25.

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a81e607ff11c6240faddac0e5508d5c45663b683eec8377dfd6e08dd131972e8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the fourth number be **x**.

⇒ Average = (10 + 20 + 25 + x) ÷ 4

⇒ 15 = (55 + x) ÷ 4

⇒ 15 × 4 = 55 + x

⇒ 60 = 55 + x

⇒ x = 60 − 55

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Observations

The total sum is always equal to **Average × Number of items** (Sum = A × n).

Net Deviation Rule

The algebraic sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always **zero**.

Change in Average

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every observation, the new average will be (Old Average ± k).

questions.question: Ravi buys an article with a discount of 25% on its marked price. He makes a profit of 10% by selling it at ₹1,320. The marked price of the article was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Marked Price (MP)** be 100 units.

**Cost Price (CP)** for Ravi = 100 − 25% of 100 = 75 units.

Ravi sells it at 10% profit ⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 75 × 110 ÷ 100 = 82.5 units.

Given SP = ₹1,320 ⇒ 82.5 units = 1320.

1 unit = 1320 ÷ 82.5 = 16.

**Marked Price** = 100 units = 100 × 16 = ₹1,600.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Discount = 25%, Profit = 10%, Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,320.

**Formulas:** CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%); MP = CP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3babd560aaa4cdb922dbdd9de03a1f588b18d59568508a9520b92263d261cfb2.png] 

⇒ First, find the **Cost Price (CP)** for Ravi: CP = 1320 × 100 ÷ 110 = ₹1,200.

⇒ This CP is the price after a 25% discount on the **Marked Price (MP)**.

⇒ Let MP be x. Then, 75% of x = 1200.

⇒ x = (1200 × 100) ÷ 75 = 16 × 100 = ₹1,600.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on an item. Discount is always calculated on the MP to arrive at the **Selling Price (SP)**.

Relation between CP and MP

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%). This direct ratio helps find MP when CP and profit/discount percentages are known.

questions.question: A positive integer N divides 228, leaving a remainder of 18. What is the greatest two-digit value of N?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The number **N** must divide (228 − 18) = 210.

According to the **remainder rule**, the divisor **N** must be greater than the remainder 18 (**N > 18**).

List factors of 210 in descending order: 210, 105, 70, 42, 35, 30, 21, 15...

The largest **two-digit factor** that satisfies **N > 18** is 70.

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Dividend = 228, Remainder = 18.

**Formula Used:** Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/75fdbba2ce506017a324fb159f074f597f4a08bbd9fc1588e08c89e4095b19d9.png] 

⇒ Let the divisor be **N** and the quotient be **q**.

⇒ 228 = (**N** × **q**) + 18

⇒ **N** × **q** = 228 − 18 = 210

⇒ This implies **N** is a factor of 210.

⇒ Factors of 210 = 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 14, 15, 21, 30, 35, 42, 70, 105, 210.

⇒ Two-digit factors of 210 are 10, 14, 15, 21, 30, 35, 42, 70.

⇒ Since the remainder is 18, **N** must be greater than 18.

⇒ Possible values for **N** = 21, 30, 35, 42, 70.

⇒ The greatest two-digit value of **N** is 70.

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Euclid's Division Lemma

For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

Divisor and Remainder Relationship

The divisor is always strictly greater than the remainder. If a number divides another with a remainder r, then the divisor must be a factor of (Dividend − r).

Finding Factors

To find all factors of a number, check divisibility by integers from 1 up to the square root of that number.

questions.question: In △ABC, ∠A = (3x-7)°, ∠B = 2∠A and ∠C = (4x+6)°. Find the value of ∠A + ∠C.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Combine all terms of **x** and constants in the **Angle Sum Property** equation:

⇒ (3x + 6x + 4x) + (−7 − 14 + 6) = 180

⇒ 13x − 15 = 180 ⇒ 13x = 195 ⇒ **x = 15**

Required sum ∠A + ∠C = (3x − 7) + (4x + 6) = 7x − 1

⇒ 7(15) − 1 = 105 − 1 = 104°

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

∠A = (3x − 7)°

∠B = 2∠A = 2(3x − 7) = (6x − 14)°

∠C = (4x + 6)°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8fa069678506d9d0e325b8e4433e78b9f734bf59e34755774c582739fa1b3737.png] 

According to the **Angle Sum Property** of a **triangle**:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ (3x − 7) + (6x − 14) + (4x + 6) = 180

⇒ 13x − 15 = 180

⇒ 13x = 180 + 15

⇒ 13x = 195

⇒ x = 195 ÷ 13

⇒ **x = 15**

Now, substitute the value of **x** to find the angles:

⇒ ∠A = 3(15) − 7 = 45 − 7 = 38°

⇒ ∠C = 4(15) + 6 = 60 + 6 = 66°

Sum of ∠A and ∠C:

⇒ ∠A + ∠C = 38° + 66° = 104°

**∴ The correct answer is 104°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the **interior angles** of any triangle is always 180°. This is a fundamental property in **Euclidean geometry**.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The **exterior angle** of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two **opposite interior angles**. For instance, Exterior ∠ACD = ∠A + ∠B.

Types of Triangles by Angles

An **Acute triangle** has all angles 90°.

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 12 days and 6 days, respectively. Both work together for 2 days and then A leaves. B completes the remaining work alone. In how many days is the whole work completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume total work as **LCM(12, 6) = 12 units**.

Efficiency: **A = 1 unit/day**, **B = 2 units/day**.

Combined efficiency of **A + B = 3 units/day**.

Work done in **2 days** = 3 × 2 = **6 units**.

Remaining work = 12 − 6 = **6 units**, completed by **B** in 6 ÷ 2 = **3 days**.

Total time taken = 2 + 3 = **5 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A** = **12 days**

Time taken by **B** = **6 days**

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **A**

 12 ÷ 12 = 1
 
 

 **B**

 12 ÷ 6 = 2
 
 

⇒ Total Work = **12 units**.

⇒ Work done by **A** and **B** in **2 days** = (1 + 2) × 2 = **6 units**.

⇒ Remaining work to be completed by **B** = 12 − 6 = **6 units**.

⇒ Time taken by **B** to finish remaining work = 6 ÷ 2 = **3 days**.

⇒ Total time for the **whole work** = Work together + Work by B alone = 2 + 3 = **5 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. If the ratio of time is x:y, the ratio of efficiency is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the work done by each individual, which is the product of their efficiency and the time they worked.

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a work in x days and B in y days, then together they can do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

questions.question: ₹5,278 is divided among X, Y, and Z in such a way that if ₹67, ₹61, and ₹68 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 8 : 20 : 5. Find X’s share after deduction.

Total amount to be divided after **deductions** = 5278 − (67 + 61 + 68) = ₹5,082.

Sum of **ratio parts** = 8 + 20 + 5 = 33 units.

Value of 1 unit = 5082 ÷ 33 = 154.

**X's share** after deduction = 8 units = 8 × 154 = ₹1,232.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,232.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total amount = ₹5,278

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of deductions = 67 + 61 + 68 = ₹196

⇒ Amount remaining after **deduction** = 5278 − 196 = ₹5,082

⇒ Let the parts be 8k, 20k, and 5k

⇒ 8k + 20k + 5k = 5082

⇒ 33k = 5082

⇒ k = 5082 ÷ 33 = 154

⇒ **X's share** after deduction = 8k = 8 × 154 = 1232

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,232.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

To divide a quantity S in the ratio a : b : c, the parts are [a/(a+b+c)] × S, [b/(a+b+c)] × S, and [c/(a+b+c)] × S respectively.

Deduction Rule

When fixed amounts are **subtracted** from the original shares to get a new ratio, always subtract the **sum** of those amounts from the total capital first.

Unitary Method in Ratios

Finding the value of '1 unit' by dividing the **total quantity** by the **sum of ratio terms** is the fastest way to calculate individual components.

questions.question: Find the third proportional to 8 and 48.2.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **third proportional** (x) to two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated using the direct formula: **x = b² ÷ a**.

Given: **a = 8** and **b = 48.2**.

Substituting the values: x = (48.2 × 48.2) ÷ 8

x = 2323.24 ÷ 8 = 290.405.

**∴ The correct answer is 290.405.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**First number (a)** = 8

**Second number (b)** = 48.2

**Formula Used:**

Three numbers a, b, and x are in **continued proportion** if the ratio of the first to the second is equal to the ratio of the second to the third: **a : b = b : x**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1971eef66de93b914f6306c72bb148be42f8c05d849c30458bbaefbcbd251b92.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 8 ÷ 48.2 = 48.2 ÷ x ⇒ 8 × x = 48.2 × 48.2 ⇒ 8x = 2323.24 ⇒ x = 2323.24 ÷ 8 ⇒ x = 290.405

**∴ The correct answer is 290.405.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b). It is the middle term when three numbers are in continued proportion.

Fourth Proportional

For four numbers **a, b, c, d** to be in proportion (a : b :: c : d), the **fourth proportional** is given by **d = (b × c) ÷ a**.

Continued Proportion

Numbers **a, b, c, d...** are said to be in **continued proportion** if a/b = b/c = c/d and so on.
